thread:
Jake (support): FYI customer AcmeAI is seeing huge p95/p99 spikes and timeouts since ~02:00 UTC. They report many 504s and long attach waits. Sample request_ids: rq_9a3b, rq_9a3f, rq_9a7c. Link to redacted convo: <https://redacted/logs/ACME/205432|logs>
Marta (oncall): Copy. Which pool are they on? any recent config changes or rollouts? :eyes:
Jake (support): Dedicated pool `dedicated-prod-3`. No recent customer-side config changes that I can see. We got an escalation email at 02:12. Ticket #INC-2054. They said latency p95 went from ~180ms -> 2.1s and p99 to 6.3s. Also saw a few 502/504s.
Ayush (eng-sre): Looking at infra metrics now. Preliminary: pool GPU utilization is high and the attach/attach-wait time spiked. Pending queue length jumped at 02:01. Autoscaler attempted scale-ups but node attach took ~40-70s causing request queueing.
Devin (eng-platform): Any errors in attach logs? cloud provider attach throttling or quota maybe. If attach fails we requeue with backoff.
Ayush (eng-sre): Yeah logs show repeated `AttachVolume` timeouts and `node-attach` retries. Provider rate-limiting visible: 429s in attach call traces. Also see kube-controller backoff: `scaleUp: waiting for resource` which delayed pod binding. Full snippet:

```
2026-02-16T02:02:14Z autoscaler: scaleUp: evaluating, desired=6, current=3
2026-02-16T02:02:15Z cloud: AttachVolume(rq_9a3b) -> 429 throttled
2026-02-16T02:02:45Z node: attach retry 3
2026-02-16T02:03:10Z pod: Pending -> Waiting for node
```

Marta (oncall): So root cause likely provider attach throttling which makes 'scale-up' look slow and increases p99. Does dedicated pool share a single AZ or volumes per node type that could be hot?
Ayush (eng-sre): Pool is region-us-west2, single subnet spread across 3 AZs but we saw most new nodes tried to attach in az-a due to scheduling bias. That increased concurrent attach traffic to limited attach endpoints. Also spot preemption earlier increased churn.
Jake (support): Customer is asking for immediate mitigations — they want stable latency now. Any quick action we can take?
Devin (eng-platform): Short-term mitigations:
- Route AcmeAI traffic to a warm spillover pool (hosted or another dedicated pool) while we stabilize the original pool.
- Increase `min_warm` for dedicated-prod-3 to keep more warm GPUs ready (temporary bump).
- Reduce attach parallelism per node group to spread attach across AZs or enable randomized AZ placement.

I can flip routing to hosted for that org for a few hours. Risk: slightly different model variant costs and billing mapping.
Ayush (eng-sre): Also immediate: increase `attach_timeout` and decrease backoff so the autoscaler retries quicker but not too aggressive. And throttle new provisioning to spread over AZs.

Devin (eng-platform): I'll run two quick changes now: 1) add routing override for customer to `hosted-fallback` 2) scale `min_warm` from 2 -> 6 for dedicated-prod-3 for next 2 hours. Anyone object?
Marta (oncall): +1 from oncall. Make sure we annotate change for rollback and add alerts to watch p95/p99 and pending queue.
Ayush (eng-sre): I can patch the autoscaler config to bias AZ selection and set `attach_parallelism`=4 to reduce spikes. Suggest keeping `attach_timeout` to 90s.

Jake (support): Customer asked for ETA on fix; I told them we're routing them to a fallback and will follow up in 30m. I'll send an intermediate update after your changes.
Devin (eng-platform): Executing now:

```
# route AcmeAI to hosted fallback
redwoodctl routing override set --org acmeai --to hosted-fallback --ttl 2h

# bump warm pool
redwoodctl pool update dedicated-prod-3 --min-warm 6 --reason "emergency bump for attach-throttle"
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for routing/override (id: dpl-78291)
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded in 18s
Customer-ops (bot): Route override applied for org acmeai -> hosted-fallback (expires 2h)

Ayush (eng-sre): I've pushed autoscaler patch (dry-run first). Command I used:

```
kubectl patch configmap/autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"attach_parallelism":"4","attach_timeout_s":"90","az_spread":"true"}}'
```

Will monitor.
Marta (oncall): Monitoring dashboards show pending queue dropped from 24 -> 2 within 60s after routing change. p95 dropped to ~220ms and p99 to ~700ms. Still slightly above baseline but much better than 6s.
Ayush (eng-sre): Good. I'm also opening a provider support ticket for attach throttling and quota increase. If provider can't raise limits we need long-term: pre-warm more nodes per AZ and change node provisioning strategy.
Devin (eng-platform): Follow-ups (post-incident):
- permanent autoscaler change to prefer AZ-level spread and cap per-AZ attach concurrency
- implement prediction-based pre-warm for known high-traffic orgs (per-org forecast)
- add alert rule: pending_queue > 10 for >1m -> automated temporary routing to hosted-fallback + paging oncall
- add quota/backoff metrics to our SLO dashboards

Jake (support): I'll update the customer: routed to hosted fallback, latency improved, we're working on long-term fix and will follow up when provider responds. Anything else before I close the escalation?
Marta (oncall): Leave it open until provider responds and autoscaler changes prove stable for 2h. Also capture all logs to the incident channel and start a short postmortem template.
Devin (eng-platform): I'll create the postmortem draft and mark action items. Assigning owner: Ayush for autoscaler config, Devin for routing automation, Jake for customer comms.
Ayush (eng-sre): Noted. I'll also run a repro test to simulate attach-throttle by firing off 50 parallel scale-ups in staging to validate the new AZ spread and attach limits.
Jake (support): Thanks all. Customer replied: "Appreciate the quick response — latency much improved." Closing note: will re-open if they see regression.
Marta (oncall): Great. Adding follow-up checklist here: 1) provider ticket ID  -> track, 2) confirm rollbacks in case of regressions, 3) confirm billing reconciliation for hosted fallback.
